fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled vCard text supplies a JSCOMPS parameter whose quoted value contains 24 semicolons (25 components). The parser accumulates the whole quoted string into state->buf and passes it as the parameter value.

Because JSCOMPS has value_kind VCARD_STRUCTURED_VALUE, the raw value string (with 24 ';' separators) is handed to vcardstructured_new_from_string(), which will create one field per ';'-separated component.

One vcardstrarray is allocated per component; st->num_fields counts components (1 initial + 1 per ';'). 25 components are requested while the field[] array only has VCARD_MAX_STRUCTURED_FIELDS (20) slots.

No bounds check against VCARD_MAX_STRUCTURED_FIELDS: for the 21st..25th component the store writes 8 bytes past the 176-byte struct (heap-buffer-overflow WRITE), corrupting adjacent heap memory and leaving st->num_fields=25 while only 20 slots exist.

When the owning vcardproperty is released, vcardparameter_free() unrefs param->structured and vcardstructured_free() iterates i < st->num_fields (25), reading st->field[20..24] which lie outside the fixed 20-entry array.

Sink: reading st->field[i] for i >= 20 consumes memory that is out of the object (or uninitialized after neighboring heap corruption), which is exactly the use-of-uninitialized-value / OOB read reported in vcardstructured_free by MSan.
